news.title: Fake Postcards Promise VA Benefits — It's a Scam Stealing Veterans' Personal Info
news.excerpt: Scammers are mailing official-looking postcards to veterans across the country, promising free monthly VA benefit payments. The postcard includes a phone number and website asking for your Social Security number or bank details to "verify eligibility." The real VA never contacts veterans this way — they already have your information on file. If you or a loved one receives one of these postcards, do not call the number or visit the website. Instead, verify any VA communication through va.gov or call 1-800-827-1000 directly. Report the scam to ReportFraud.ftc.gov. — Source: FTC, August 24, 2026

news.title: Brushing Scams: Why Random Packages Are Showing Up at Your Door
news.excerpt: A package shows up on your porch you never ordered. The FTC warned on August 20 that this is a "brushing" scam — sellers send you free junk using your name so they can post a fake five-star review in your name. Some packages include QR codes that lead to fake websites designed to steal your information. If you receive a package you did not order, do not scan any codes inside. Check your online accounts for unfamiliar orders and report it free at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

news.title: Fake Bill-Payment Websites Are Tricking You Through Search Ads
news.excerpt: The FTC just warned that scammers are buying fake ads at the top of Google and Bing that look like your electric company, insurance provider, or bank. You search for "pay my light bill," click the first result, enter your account number and card, and the money goes to a crook instead of your real company. Always scroll past the ads and look for the official web address you already know — or call the number on your paper bill. Report fraud at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. (Source: FTC.gov, August 17, 2026)

news.title: Microsoft Edge Browser Security Update — Check Yours in 30 Seconds Free
news.excerpt: Microsoft pushed a fresh security patch to Edge this week that closes several vulnerabilities attackers are actively exploiting through malicious websites. If your Edge browser is out of date, simply visiting the wrong page could let someone run code on your computer. Here's the fix — it's free and takes 30 seconds: open Microsoft Edge, click the three dots in the top right corner, choose Help and feedback, then About Microsoft Edge. The browser will show your current version and update automatically if it's not current. I do this check on every computer that comes into the shop, and I'm always surprised how many are months behind. Don't be one of them — check it now. (Source: Microsoft Security Response Center, August 2026)

news.title: Healthcare Company CareCloud Confirms Data Breach Affecting 3.7 Million Patients
news.excerpt: Healthcare technology company CareCloud confirmed a massive data breach that exposed personal information of 3.7 million patients, according to a report by BleepingComputer on August 19, 2026. If you or a family member received care from a medical provider that uses CareCloud systems, your name, contact details, and health-related information may have been compromised. Here's what to do right now: call your healthcare provider's office and ask if they use CareCloud, then place a free fraud alert on your credit reports by calling Equifax at 1-800-525-6285, Experian at 1-888-397-3742, or TransUnion at 1-800-680-7289.

posts.title: Windows 11 August update causes games to crash and PCs to reboot — Microsoft is working on a patch
posts.summary: If your PC crashes, freezes, or reboots by itself after the August Windows update, you're not alone — Microsoft has confirmed the issue and a proper fix is on the way. Don't uninstall the update, which leaves you vulnerable to 400+ security holes; just wait for Microsoft's patch within the next few weeks.
posts.truth: I've been seeing this all week in the shop — customers come in thinking their PC is dying, but it's actually the August update conflicting with an old RGB lighting driver. The problem is real but temporary. Microsoft's proper patch should arrive soon, and in the meantime the affected games and apps still work fine on most PCs. The only people who should be worried are folks who rely on specific gaming software for work.

posts.title: CISA Flags 4 Actively Exploited Flaws — Update Your Mac and Windows Now
posts.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added four new actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on August 18. Two affect Apple Macs and two affect Windows. Update macOS at System Settings > General > Software Update and Windows at Settings > Windows Update tonight.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize that when CISA adds a flaw to its "Known Exploited Vulnerabilities" list, it means hackers are already using it right now — not someday, not theoretically, right now. The Apple macOS flaw lets someone on your network authenticate to your Mac's screen sharing without proper credentials. On Windows, a flaw in a core networking service could let an attacker take over your computer with admin-level control. I see this all the time: customers come in two weeks after an alert saying "I thought it was fine." By then the damage is done. The honest answer is: if your computer is on and connected to the internet, you need to update it tonight.

posts.title: Stop Windows from begging you to buy Microsoft 365 — turn off the subscription nag screens
posts.summary: Press the Windows key, type **Notifications** and press Enter. Scroll down and turn off notifications from **Microsoft 365 (Office)** and **Get Help**. That kills the pop-ups permanently — takes 30 seconds.
posts.truth: I see this all the time — people think their computer is broken because it keeps popping up windows telling them to "Try Microsoft 365" or "Renew your subscription." It's not broken. Windows is just advertising to you. Most people don't realize that these nag screens are built-in notifications, and you can turn them off the same way you'd silence a chatty app. The honest answer is Microsoft wants your $100 a year, so they're going to keep asking. But you don't have to listen.

posts.title: Microsoft Edge just got a security update — check yours free in 30 seconds at edge://settings/help
posts.summary: Microsoft pushed a fresh security patch to Edge this week. Open Microsoft Edge, click the three dots in the top right, choose Help and feedback, then About Microsoft Edge — it will show your current version and update automatically if it's not current. Takes 30 seconds.
posts.truth: I see this all the time. Someone tells me "I never get viruses" while running a browser that hasn't updated in three months. Here's the honest truth: you don't get a virus the moment a security hole opens — you get it weeks later, after the bad guys figure out how to use it. That's why Microsoft pushes these updates fast. Most people don't realize Edge updates itself, but only if you open the browser and let it check. If you've been ignoring that little "update available" bar at the top, you're leaving the door open. I check Edge on every machine that comes through the shop — it takes 30 seconds and could save you from a real headache.

posts.title: Government warns ransomware gangs are targeting Windows computers right now — Windows Update keeps you safe
posts.summary: CISA (the government's cybersecurity agency) confirmed that ransomware gangs are actively using a Windows flaw to take full control of computers. Open Settings, click Windows Update, and click "Check for updates" — it takes 2 minutes and keeps you safe.
posts.truth: I see this every week at the shop. Someone clicks a bad link and suddenly all their photos, documents, and tax files are locked up with a ransom note on the screen. Most people think it only happens to big companies, but ransomware gangs target regular people too — your personal files are worth money to them. The good news: Microsoft already fixed this months ago. If your Windows Update is current, you're already protected. If it's not — fix it tonight.

posts.title: Chrome 153 ships with a critical security patch — take 30 seconds to update now
posts.summary: Open Chrome, click the three dots at top right, click Help, then About Google Chrome — the update installs automatically when you open that page.
posts.truth: Google just patched a critical memory bug in Chrome 153 that could let a bad website take over your computer. The update is free, takes 30 seconds, and you don't need to do anything except open the update page. I check this for every customer who comes in — it's one of the fastest ways to stay safe online. Most people don't realize their browser is the front door to their computer, and keeping it updated is the easiest protection you have.

posts.title: Patch My PC Home Updater Updates 500 Apps Free at patchmypc.com
posts.summary: Download Patch My PC Home Updater free at patchmypc.com, run it, and click Scan — it finds every outdated app on your PC and updates them all in one click. It supports over 500 apps including Chrome, Firefox, Zoom, VLC, 7-Zip, iTunes, Skype, and more.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize that old versions of programs are the #1 way hackers get into your computer. Every outdated app is an open door. I see this all the time: customers have the same version of Chrome from six months ago, or their Zoom is three updates behind. The honest answer is: nobody wants to sit there updating 15 apps one by one. Patch My PC solves that. You download it once, run it, and it handles everything. It is not installed permanently — it runs like a quick checkup tool. I use it in the shop on every machine that comes through.

posts.title: Turn your old scanner into a clean PDF maker — NAPS2 is free and has no watermarks
posts.summary: Download **NAPS2** (Not Another PDF Scanner 2) free at **naps2.org**. Plug in your scanner, open NAPS2, click the green **Scan** button, and save your document as a PDF or image file. No account, no watermarks, no ads, no subscription.
posts.truth: I see this every week — someone bought a nice printer with a scanner and they can't figure out how to scan a document to their computer. The software that came with the printer is confusing, asks for an account, or puts a watermark on every page. Here's the truth: you don't need the manufacturer's software at all. NAPS2 works with almost every scanner made in the last 20 years, and it does one thing — turns your paper into a clean digital file. No strings attached.

posts.title: Find any file in a second — Everything Search by Voidtools is free and finds what Windows Search misses at voidtools.com
posts.summary: Windows Search is slow and sometimes misses files entirely. Everything Search by Voidtools indexes your entire drive the moment you install it and finds any file the instant you type its name. Download it free from voidtools.com — no account needed, no ads, takes 2 minutes to install.
posts.truth: I recommend this to almost every customer who walks in frustrated because they can't find a file. Here's what most people don't realize: Windows Search indexes only some files and sometimes takes minutes to return results. Everything indexes everything — every file on every drive — and shows results as you type. I've watched people spend 10 minutes looking for a document that Everything finds in half a second. It's free, it's tiny, it doesn't slow your computer down, and once you use it you'll never go back to Windows Search. I install it on every machine I set up in the shop.

posts.title: Adobe Firefly now generates music, speech, and sound effects free — try it at firefly.adobe.com
posts.summary: Adobe's free AI tool Firefly can now create background music, voice narration, and sound effects from a simple text description. Go to firefly.adobe.com, sign up free with any email, and click "Generate Audio" — no music skills needed, and you get free tries every day.
posts.truth: I'm not a music guy, but I had a customer last week who needed a short background track for a church slideshow. She typed "gentle piano, 30 seconds" into Firefly and had something she could use in about a minute. Most people don't realize these tools exist — they think making audio requires expensive software or a recording studio. You don't. Adobe gives you free daily generations, and it's enough for most personal projects. The honest answer is: for a church presentation, a family video, or a school project, this is more than good enough.
